clue.text: Cast having finished in audition

indicators.note: an audition is a hearing, so these words ask for a word that is heard rather than seen

parts.note: someone who has finished is through

explanation.surface: An actor's casting is decided once the audition is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cast' looks like a theatre company, but it is the past tense of throw.
explanation.definitionFit: To cast a ball is to throw it, so the past tense of cast fits the past tense of throw.

clue.text: Expression of surprise seen in paintings, some painted by Gauguin

indicators.note: seen in tells us one piece appears inside another

parts.note: Titians are paintings by the Venetian master Titian
ah is a cry of surprise

explanation.surface: Surprise at finding, among some paintings, works by Gauguin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'paintings' looks like a general word, but it needs works by one painter; Titian was a Venetian master of the Renaissance.
explanation.definitionFit: Gauguin painted many Polynesian people in Tahiti, so his subjects were often islanders of Tahiti.

clue.text: Provide new weaponry, with specialist troops grabbing attention

indicators.note: grabbing means seizing and holding, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: RM is the Royal Marines, an elite force
to give an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Elite troops seize attention as they get new weapons.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' only joins the definition to the wordplay; the Royal Marines are Britain's commando force.
explanation.definitionFit: To rearm is to equip again with weapons.

clue.text: Use pedestrian method at bridge for easy win

definitions.meaning: to cross a bridge on foot is to walk across it
a victory won with no real contest

explanation.definitionFit: Walk over is crossing on foot; a walkover is a victory won without effort.

clue.text: Split and broken apart, in beginning

indicators.note: in tells us the rearranged word goes inside the word for beginning

parts.note: a seed is the beginning from which something grows

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of the word apart are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something split and smashed apart right at its origin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges the word apart, and 'in' sets the result between the two Es of the word for beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: Split as an adjective describes things that have been divided or parted from each other.

clue.text: Number derivable from points on graph

indicators.note: derivable from says the answer can be drawn out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A figure worked out from the points on a graph.
explanation.walkthrough: 'derivable from' points to the run of letters inside 'points on graph'.
explanation.definitionFit: A number in music is a piece or tune, so a song is a number.

clue.text: Nicer soups cooked in kitchen

indicators.note: cooked means altered or concocted, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Tastier soups prepared in the kitchen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges NICER SOUPS. 'Kitchen' is orchestra slang for the percussion section.
explanation.definitionFit: Players call the orchestra's percussion section the kitchen, for its pots-and-pans array of instruments.

clue.text: Prepare to publish left-wing legislation

parts.note: red is the colour of left-wing politics
an Act is a piece of legislation

explanation.surface: Getting ready to issue socialist legislation.
explanation.definitionFit: To redact is to edit text into a form ready for publishing.

clue.text: Representative that loudly expresses rage, initially, about party line

indicators.note: about means around, so the initials go round the other pieces
initially means the first letters of the four words before it are taken

parts.note: a rave is a large dance party

explanation.surface: An MP who shouts in fury when the party line is mentioned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes the first letters of 'that loudly expresses rage', TLER; 'about' puts that around RAVE and L. 'Representative' is a commercial traveller, a sales rep.
explanation.definitionFit: A commercial traveller is a sales representative who visits customers on the road.

clue.text: Kind of clue like this, about river in flood

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: this clue is a Down clue

explanation.surface: A clue type described while a river floods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts DOWN around R.
explanation.definitionFit: To drown fields is to submerge them, which is to flood them.

clue.text: Star performer, understanding craft

parts.note: a head for something is an understanding of it, a sense of mind or intelligence
a liner is an ocean-going craft or ship

explanation.surface: A star turn who also knows a good deal about crafts.
explanation.definitionFit: A headliner is the main act on the bill, the star the audience has come to see.

clue.text: Harsh legislator returned ring with diamond, say

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the pieces are read from end to start

parts.note: a ring is round, the shape of the letter O
a diamond is one kind of playing card, hence say

explanation.surface: A stern lawmaker sends back an engagement ring set with a diamond.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returned' reverses O plus CARD to give DRACO.
explanation.definitionFit: Draco was the Athenian lawgiver whose severe code gave English the word draconian.

clue.text: Grave situation, nothing unknown for tough girl

parts.note: a tomb is where a grave is situated, a burial place
nothing is zero, the letter O
Y is an algebraic unknown, as in x and y

explanation.surface: A grim predicament leaves a hardy girl with nothing she does not know.
explanation.definitionFit: A tomboy is a girl who acts in a rough, boisterous way usually associated with boys.

clue.text: Full form of meal never freely available, it's said

definitions.text: Full form of meal never freely available, it's said

parts.words: Full form of meal never freely available, it's said
parts.note: the proverb says there is no such thing as a free lunch; the full, formal name of that meal is wanted

explanation.surface: The formal name for a meal that, proverbially, nobody ever gets for free.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying is 'there's no such thing as a free lunch'; lunch is the short form, so the full form is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: Luncheon is the formal, older word of which lunch is the clipped everyday form.

clue.text: Bit of Norfolk dialect for an old weapon

parts.note: the Norfolk Broads are waterways, and a word of their local speech could be called a term from the Broads

explanation.surface: A term from East Anglian dialect for an old weapon.
explanation.walkthrough: The Norfolk Broads are lakes and rivers in eastern England.
explanation.definitionFit: A broadsword is a heavy sword with a broad blade, an old weapon.

clue.text: Has true aim misrepresented? That's inept

indicators.note: misrepresented means shown wrongly, so the letters of the phrase are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone claims a true aim, but the misrepresentation looks clumsy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misrepresented' rearranges the ten letters of HAS TRUE AIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Amateurish work is unskilful and clumsy, as inept work is.

clue.text: Establish new sectarian organization

indicators.note: new means made fresh, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: Founding a new sectarian organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges SECTARIAN; 'organization' adds to the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a fact is to find it out for certain, to ascertain it.

clue.text: Shot relatively small number, about about 50

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: few means a relatively small number
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A marksman fired only a modest number of times, about fifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts FEW around L.
explanation.definitionFit: Shot in the sense of moved very fast, as in time shot by, means the same as flew.

clue.text: European or American partners getting more serious

parts.note: W and E, West and East, are partners at the bridge table
sterner means more serious or severe

explanation.surface: Partners from either side of the Atlantic become grimmer.
explanation.walkthrough: In bridge the four players are North, South, East and West, with East and West partners.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone from the western world, Europe or America, is a westerner.

clue.text: Take away a couple of vehicles turning up on time

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning up means each piece is written bottom to top

parts.note: a bus is one vehicle
a cart is the second vehicle

explanation.surface: Two vehicles arrive on time to take something away.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'turning up' reads each vehicle bottom to top, in place; 'on' just puts the time letter after them.
explanation.definitionFit: To take away one number from another is to subtract it.

clue.text: Devastate in fire

definitions.meaning: to ... a town is to plunder and lay it waste
to fire someone is to dismiss them from a job

explanation.definitionFit: Sack means both to plunder a captured city and to dismiss an employee.

clue.text: Soldier works for large-scale military exercise

parts.note: a man is a soldier in the ranks, as in officers and men
oeuvres is French for works, used in English for an artist's body of work

explanation.surface: A soldier's duties are a large military exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: Manoeuvres are large-scale training exercises by troops, ships or aircraft.

clue.text: Musician in film, starting with piano

indicators.note: starting with puts the piano abbreviation at the front

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, softly
a layer is a thin film, as of oil

explanation.surface: A musician in a film whose career began at the piano.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who plays an instrument is a player, a musician.

clue.text: Good teacher has reason for unclear view about exam

indicators.note: about means around, so one piece is placed round the other

parts.note: mist makes the view unclear
an oral is a spoken exam

explanation.surface: A fine teacher can explain why an exam feels hazy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has reason for' only joins the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A moralist teaches or preaches about right conduct, a teacher of what is good.

clue.text: Polite form of address in Mothers' Union?

parts.note: ma is a word for mother
a dam is an animal's mother

explanation.surface: A courteous way to address members of a women's organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Union' just joins the two mothers. The Mothers' Union is a Christian women's charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam is a respectful way of addressing a woman.

clue.text: Keep paper together that's the main thing

definitions.meaning: the wire clip that fastens sheets of paper
a ... is a principal item, as rice is a ... food

explanation.surface: Clipping papers together is the main task.
explanation.definitionFit: A staple is a wire paper fastener and also a basic, principal commodity or feature.

clue.text: Political leader isn't commonly put in the picture

indicators.note: leader means the first letter of the word political is taken

parts.note: ain't is the colloquial form of isn't

explanation.surface: A party leader is not usually kept informed.
explanation.definitionFit: To paint someone is to depict them, literally putting them in a picture.

clue.text: Alcoholic drink knocking out one very large group

indicators.note: knocking out means removing, so a letter is taken from the drink

parts.note: bevvy is British slang for an alcoholic drink
V is an abbreviation for very; one says just one of the two Vs goes

explanation.surface: An alcoholic drink knocks out one member of a very large crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: BEVVY is British slang for booze; dropping one V gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A bevy is a large group or flock, especially of people or birds.

clue.text: Apart from Evelyn, nobody wrote one

definitions.text: Apart from Evelyn, nobody wrote one

parts.words: Apart from Evelyn, nobody wrote one
parts.note: John Evelyn kept a famous journal, and Grossmith's novel is the journal of 'a Nobody'

explanation.surface: Seemingly a claim that only Evelyn ever wrote such a thing.
explanation.walkthrough: John Evelyn was a 17th-century English diarist; The Diary of a Nobody is a comic Victorian novel by George and Weedon Grossmith.
explanation.definitionFit: Both Evelyn and the fictional Nobody kept a daily journal of their lives.

clue.text: Old form of exercise helping medical treatment

parts.note: PE is physical education, exercise at school
a ration is a helping or allowance of food

explanation.surface: An old style of exercise helps with medical treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgery done on a patient is an operation, a form of medical treatment.

clue.text: Companion the narrator had in battle on island

indicators.note: in an across clue, battle on island places the battle piece after the island piece

parts.note: Man is the Isle of Man in the Irish Sea

indicators.note: in tells us one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a fray is a fight or battle
the narrator would say I'd, short for I had

explanation.surface: A storyteller's companion during a fight on an island.
explanation.walkthrough: Man Friday is Robinson Crusoe's companion, and Crusoe narrates the novel himself, so 'the narrator' fits the surface too.
explanation.definitionFit: A man Friday is a loyal helper or companion, after Crusoe's servant.

clue.text: Starts off this unusual type of reading as teacher

indicators.note: starts off means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A teacher begins with this odd kind of reading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Starts off' takes the first letters of 'this unusual type of reading'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor is a private teacher or one supervising a small group of students.
